{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZX3OSg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhC_MFk", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 67, "title": "Use one stable historical calendar across session, forum, mail, conference and OLT dates", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `0dd9facabcd2974a5b77f0aee31e81ae50ac8880`, residents inhabit late 1996, but service-generated dates expose the contemporary operational calendar:

- `src/connection.ts` prints session ISO timestamps and `(UTC)` during entry.
- `src/forums.ts` formats `simulation.simulatedAt ?? createdAt` directly.
- `src/mail.ts` exposes those effective timestamps in lists and details.
- `src/conference.ts` prints contribution `createdAt` directly.
- `src/olt.ts` slices operational timestamps into conversation lines and labels them UTC.

A connected visit therefore contradicts its historical setting. This advances an explicitly deferred fidelity gap, rather than correcting a regression in the preceding implementations.

## Expected outcome

All five surfaces use one stable, world-specific historical presentation calendar. A newly initialized world begins in late November 1996; subsequent activity advances consistently with elapsed source time. Existing records retain stable displayed dates across navigation, reload, reconnect and backup restoration.

Actual stored timestamps, AI scheduling, consent, retention, ordering and read-state semantics remain operational. Authored date strings and user text retain their own dates. Modern Settings may continue showing actual operational times.

## Context

**Historical evidence, inspected 2026-10-23:**

- The [preserved login excerpt](https://akibabara.com/blog/4569.html), published 2010-09-22 and containing a session dated 1995-04-02, displays previous-use-end and current-use-start dates. Confidence is high about the preserved contents and moderate about adjacent-year applicability. It is incomplete and does not establish the 1996 wording, timezone or a fictional epoch.
- The [author-preserved PC-VAN course archive](https://someya.sakura.ne.jp/poem/tansi/tansimain.html) identifies its SIG origin and contains target-year contribution headers, including a notice dated 1996-08-07. These support two-digit year/month/day and time in forum headers. Confidence is high about the displayed structure, with limitations from later preservation and encoding damage. Another SIG's records cannot authenticate DAISIZEN mail, conference or OLT layouts. Copy no messages or identities.

**Accepted reconstruction:** use fixed JST for simulated service dates. Define a source anchor `A` and a historical anchor `H`, then project operational instants using `H + (instant - A)`. Choose `H` at the corresponding weekday and JST time of day in 1996-11-18 through 1996-11-24. This deliberately fictional week preserves ordinary time-of-day and weekday relationships without changing resident schedules. Advance through normal Gregorian midnight, month and year boundaries, including into 1997; do not wrap or replace the year independently on each render. Exact anchoring and non-forum date formatting are reconstructed, not authenticated host behavior.

Reuse the durable `community-world.createdAt` as the source anchor where suitable. If legacy/imported data requires additional mapping metadata, keep it small, validated and included in the existing backup mechanism. Initialization must be stable and must not overwrite existing world provenance. A dated legacy backup lacking an anchor needs a documented deterministic fallback derived from its records, rather than its import time. An entirely undated world may initialize once on activation.

Preserve already-historical legacy effective instants in 1996–1997 without applying the offset again. This is a conservative import assumption, not proof of historical authenticity. A target-era world marker must not be mistaken for the operational clock anchor for newly created contemporary events. Document and test this distinction. Ordinary `simulation.simulatedAt` represents a catch-up event on the operational source clock and must receive the same projection as other operational activity.

Live repository searches found no open Issues or PRs. [Session entry #61](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/61), [resident setting #63](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/63), [library/OSL #59](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/59) and [conference #65](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/65) explicitly deferred the general calendar. [Starter history #37](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/37) already establishes durable world anchoring.

[PR #66](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/66) and `docs/validation.md` report 242 passing tests and 29 subsequent focused checks, including production builds. Those are Coordinator records. This research graph ran no builds or tests.

Scope is date presentation and the minimal persistence needed to stabilize it. Information services, host paging, historical command recovery and resident generation behavior remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement one shared calendar projection and formatting policy used by entry, forum reading, mail lists/details, conference reading and both live/replayed OLT lines. Wire it through `main.ts`, navigation and command dispatch as needed; avoid independent year substitutions or transcript-wide text replacement.
- [ ] Implement the disclosed anchor, JST and rollover policy above. Mapping remains fixed for a world and agrees across tabs. Reuse existing world metadata where sufficient; any added metadata has strict validation, atomic initialization and backup/import/reset support. No configurable calendar subsystem or new dependency is required.
- [ ] Specify the legacy fallback algorithm in code/docs and test it. Restoring the same dated legacy backup at different wall-clock times produces the same dates for its existing records. Already-historical legacy instants are not offset twice; new operational activity still receives a valid historical projection. Repeated rendering never compounds an offset.
- [ ] Keep `simulation.simulatedAt ?? createdAt` as the effective event-time selection for forum/mail activity. Project that selected instant once. Preserve the distinction between catch-up event time and actual commit time, including pending runs created before calendar initialization.
- [ ] Preserve raw `createdAt`, simulation metadata, session timestamps, mail `readAt`, IDs, numbering, reply references and existing ordering. Calendar rendering must not rewrite records, schedule from historical time, change OLT expiry/retention, or alter AI activity watermarks and due times. Normal existing send/read/session operations may still make their usual changes.
- [ ] Missing previous logout remains explicitly unrecorded; reload must not invent one. Replace obsolete UTC labels where simulated dates now use JST. Use concise Japanese dates, retaining the existing forum header structure. Keep OSL date-only metadata, authored fixture dates and all titles/bodies unchanged; format historical canonical instants without calendar translation. Modern Settings retains truthful operational timestamps.
- [ ] Add deterministic checks using the existing Playwright facilities. Cover one controlled instant across all five services, an older AI catch-up instant, JST midnight, month/year rollover, a valid leap-day input, different browser timezones, missing logout and preservation of literal date-like user text. Assert expected values independently of the production formatter.
- [ ] Cover a production-browser journey through entry, forum reading/contribution, local mail, conference and OLT without real inference. Verify existing-message display stability after reload and backup/restore; legacy and already-historical imports; reset creating a fresh mapping; and consistency across tabs. Preserve existing atomic-import rollback, stale-world, empty-world and consent coverage. Do not require unchanged session/history fields when the journey legitimately updates them.
- [ ] Update affected usage/storage/terminal documentation, Settings/About and research notes. Record inspected sources, confidence, the fictional epoch/JST/import assumptions and the distinction between displayed and operational time. Supersede stale claims that ordinary service dates intentionally show actual UTC, while preserving the historical record of earlier scopes. Do not add routine provenance paragraphs to service screens.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; the current Playwright configuration includes TypeScript checking and the production build. Retain functional, storage, consent, composition, IME, scrolling, progressive output and skip regressions. Review the final diff and `git diff --check`, and report actual results. No model download, real inference, new framework or hardware check is required.

## Optional validation

A short manual connected visit may assess readability and date-line width at 320px. Further historical research into timezone and service-specific date layouts is useful but does not block this explicitly disclosed reconstruction.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge through existing local tooling.
